attentive: Forward gaze and relaxed or slightly lifted mouth.
Neutral attention; low. Service, listening or a routine reply. Avoid a crisis reaction.
amused: Lifted mouth corner or hand near a smile.
Amusement, sometimes dry; medium. A private joke or teasing retort. Avoid grief.
annoyed: Drawn brows and open protesting mouth.
Irritation; medium. Intrusion or aggravation. Avoid reassurance.
angry: Steep brows and an open mouth or pronounced frown.
Anger; high. Reprimand or confrontation. Avoid casual service.
apologetic: Raised inner brows and small downturned mouth.
Regret or concern; medium. Apology or refusal. Avoid triumphant lines.
appalled: Open mouth and worried, lifted brows.
Alarm or revulsion; high. A startling offence. Avoid agreement.
asleep: Eyes closed and slack open mouth.
Sleep; low. Dozing. Avoid an active argument.
awake: Wide eyes, open mouth and marks beside the head.
Startle; high. A sudden wake-up. Avoid composed explanation.
big-excited-smile: Wide open grin, raised hand and accent marks.
blushing: Closed, curved eyes, small smile and coloured cheeks.
Shy pleasure with embarrassment; medium. Affection. Avoid indifference.
condescending: Raised brows and open grin behind spectacles.
Patronising amusement; medium. A lecture or self-satisfied correction. Avoid sincere contrition.
conspiratorial: Hand raised near the mouth and lowered eyelids.
Secrecy or confidence; medium. A whispered aside. Avoid public panic.
contemplative: Fingers near the chin under the cow skull.
Reflection; low. Parables or deliberation. Avoid an explosive reaction.
current-smile: Small curved mouth and steady brows behind spectacles.
Professional composure; low. A diplomatic explanation. Avoid terror.
deadpan: Level mouth or restrained frown, posture held still.
Flat delivery or dryness; low. A procedural or understated reply. Avoid a jubilant outburst.
defiant: Defiance with irritation; medium. Refusal. Avoid conciliation.
delighted: Closed crescent eyes and broad open grin.
Delight; high. Celebration or pleased recognition. Avoid suspicion.
demonic-angry: Sharp inward brows and bared teeth.
Fury; high. A sharp denial or threat. Avoid restrained instruction.
despondent: Eyes lowered or shut, drooping brows and frown.
Dejection; medium. Resignation. Avoid energetic disagreement.
devious: Cunning with amusement; medium. Hinting or calculation. Avoid open distress.
disappointed: Disappointment; medium. A let-down. Avoid enthusiasm.
displeased: Angled brows with a definite frown.
dismayed: Closed eyes and a deep frown.
Dismay; medium. Defeat or regret. Avoid boasting.
distressed: Clenched mouth, taut eyes and a sweat mark.
Distress; high. Fear of consequences. Avoid quiet hospitality.
drowsy: Heavy eyelids and slack, open mouth.
Sleepiness; medium. Groggy responses. Avoid alert scrutiny.
evil-laugh: Inward brows and broad open grin.
Menacing amusement; high. A gloating punchline. Avoid sympathetic advice.
exasperated: Open mouth and expression of strained, closed or upturned eyes.
Frustration or exhaustion; high. Repetition or disbelief. Avoid relaxed agreement.
excited: Wide open mouth with a smile; some variants add accent marks.
Excitement; high. An announcement or invitation. Avoid solemn remarks.
exuberant: Open grin and uplifted features beneath a top hat.
Showmanship; high. A pitch. Avoid private regret.
flustered: Sweat mark, coloured cheeks and round mouth.
Embarrassment with alarm; high. Being caught out. Avoid deliberate menace.
formal: Discipline; low. An official greeting or report. Avoid a joke carried by expression.
frown: Downturned mouth and angled brows behind sunglasses.
frowning: Lowered brows and downturned mouth over the pillory.
Disapproval with strain; medium. Objection or indignity. Avoid delight.
happy: Small smile or open smiling mouth, shoulders relaxed.
Pleasure; low to medium. Agreement or genial greeting. Avoid warning.
hurried: Sweat mark and tense smile, still holding the drink.
Haste with worry; medium. Pressed service. Avoid leisurely confidence.
impressed: Lifted brows, wide eyes and small round mouth.
Surprise or admiration; medium. An unexpected result. Avoid bored dismissal.
insulted: Arched brows and open protest behind spectacles.
Indignation with surprise; high. A personal affront. Avoid neutral accounting.
irritated: Irritation; medium. Inconvenience. Avoid warm praise.
laugh: Eyes squeezed into arcs and smiling mouth.
Amusement; medium. A dry laugh. Avoid threat without comic intent.
laughing: Curved or closed eyes and wide grin.
Laughter; high. A punchline or celebration. Avoid sincere sympathy.
listening: Two-way radio held close, mouth level.
Concentration; low. Receiving instructions. Avoid a shouted response.
microphone: Microphone raised and wide open grin.
Performance excitement; high. Addressing the room. Avoid whispered remarks.
milk-drool: Eyes closed, milk visibly trailing from the mouth.
Sleepy loss of composure; medium. Dormant or comic interruption. Avoid an attentive reply.
nervous: Worried brows, tight mouth and sometimes a sweat mark.
Unease; medium. Hesitation or awkwardness. Avoid assured delivery.
notebook: Eyes lowered towards an open book, pen and both hands visible.
Concentrated enquiry; low. Taking notes or reviewing results. Avoid a sudden outburst.
offended: Lifted or angled brows, tight mouth; the bartender has a huff mark.
Indignation; medium. A slight or breach of etiquette. Avoid heartfelt thanks.
pleased: Soft smile and often closed crescent eyes.
Contentment; medium. Appreciation or approval. Avoid bad news.
polite: Courtesy; low. Formal service. Avoid grief.
protective: Angled brows, open mouth and fist raised.
Defensiveness with fear or anger; high. Protecting possessions. Avoid relaxation.
radio: Radio raised and open speaking mouth.
Urgent communication; medium. Calling in a report. Avoid silent listening.
reading-figures: Open book held in front, eyes directed down.
Calculation or concentration; low. Financial figures. Avoid a shock reaction.
relieved: Small smile below lifted, soft brows.
Relief with residual concern; low. A reprieve. Avoid escalating danger.
reserved: Small, closed mouth with partly lowered lids.
Reserve or mild amusement; low. Wary agreement. Avoid euphoria.
sad: Downturned mouth and low or closed eyes.
Sadness; medium. Loss or regret. Avoid gloating.
self-assured: Confidence; low. A practiced explanation. Avoid panic.
self-assured-smirk: One corner of the mouth lifts; eyes slightly narrowed.
Arrogance or dry amusement; medium. A smug correction. Avoid sincere distress.
serene: Soft smile and relaxed shoulders beneath the skull.
Calm; low. A quiet greeting. Avoid agitation.
sheepish: Embarrassment; medium. Backpedalling. Avoid unqualified authority.
shocked: Rounded mouth, raised brows or emphatic head marks.
Surprise or alarm; high. An abrupt revelation. Avoid composed indifference.
sipping: Glass raised to the lips and eyes closed.
Contentment; low. A drink or a pause. Avoid a long uninterrupted speech.
skeptical: One brow set or raised, with lowered lids or a flat mouth.
Doubt or suspicion; medium. Testing a claim. Avoid unconditional approval.
smirk: A slight sideways smile under sunglasses.
Playful confidence; low. A quip. Avoid anguish.
smug: Unilateral smile and relaxed or partly closed lids.
Smug satisfaction; medium. A boast. Avoid a frightened confession.
speaking: Mouth open in a small oval, shoulders squared.
Neutral assertion; low. A spoken instruction. Avoid signalling quiet assent.
stern: Straight or downturned mouth and firm eyebrows.
Stern disapproval; medium. A boundary or demand. Avoid warmth.
stressed: Raised inner brows and open, anxious mouth.
Anxiety; high. Exposure or an urgent request. Avoid composure.
suspicious: Uneven brow or sidelong set of the face.
Distrust; medium. A challenge. Avoid open celebration.
thinking: A raised brow, angled gaze, pursed mouth or hand near the face.
Reflection or uncertainty; low. A pause to consider. Avoid a determined outburst.
tousled: Loose hair strands around the face and a half smile.
Smug relaxation; low. Post-encounter dialogue. Avoid a formal first greeting.
warning: Open palm raised and mouth open beneath the skull.
Caution or insistence; medium. A warning. Avoid quiet assent.
weary: Fatigue with resignation; medium. Weariness. Avoid enthusiasm.
welcoming: Open smile and service posture with a glass or tray.
Hospitality; medium. An offered drink. Avoid rebuke.
winded: Drooping eyelids, open mouth, sweat and a drawn breath mark.
Physical fatigue; high. After exertion. Avoid cool deliberation.
wistful: Small hesitant smile with lifted inner brows.
Nostalgia with sadness; low. A recollection. Avoid rage.
worried: Inner brows raised and mouth open or downturned.
Concern or fear; medium. Uncertain news. Avoid a boast.
wry-smile: Small smile tucked beneath the skull, head held steady.
Dry amusement; low. A sly observation. Avoid grief.
alarmed: Raised inner brows and round open mouth.
Alarm; high. Shock or fear. Avoid calm reflection.
hurt: A visible tear and downturned mouth as Lin holds the tray.
Hurt or sadness; medium. Betrayal or rejection. Avoid casual service.
